name: New Zealand
kernel_gaps: eligibility-window credit (IETC: nil below $24,000 and above $70,000, abated 13 c above $66,000; Credit has phase-in/withdrawal but no lower eligibility floor)
shared abatement of two credits (FTC abates first, the remainder off the IWTC; proved equal to one abatement of the sum)
guaranteed-income top-up (MFTC: threshold minus income after tax, a 100 % withdrawal by construction)
credit barred by entitlement to another benefit (IETC while WFF > 0)
day-weighted composite year (2024-25: composite rates and composite IETC/IWTC/MFTC over 121 + 244 days)
money in cents (NZ computes in cents; Out is whole units, so cents are kept in detail)

headline: New Zealand's 2025-26 tax and Working for Families match the OECD and IRD's PAYE tables exactly (69,228 cells; table = statute proved for every income), but the minimum family tax credit band has a 101.67 % effective marginal rate (113.67 % with a student loan), WFF's bar on the IETC makes a $1,040 notch, the OECD leaves out the ACC levy, and IRD's 2025-26 guidance has five inconsistent figures or formulas.
year_note: 2025 (income year 1 April 2025 - 31 March 2026 = the OECD's 2025; 2024-25 composite year also modelled)
